summary: Point-B (post-implementation) review of Task 5's test suite: all 16 named TDD-Anchor tests exist and genuinely test their claimed behavior (verified by reading every assertion and by running the full suite green with 0 failures across handler/config/cmd/service packages). All 5 findings from the design-round review (test-reviewer-design-1.json: 3 major, 2 minor) are confirmed genuinely fixed, not just reportedly fixed -- for the 3 highest-risk ones I mutated the corresponding production code and confirmed the exact test that was supposed to catch it does fail, then reverted byte-identical (git diff clean): (1) TestAccessHandler_RepositoryFailureAfterGatePasses, added with per-login getErrByLogin/listErr/setAccessErr stub knobs, genuinely exercises AccessHandler's own error-wrapping on ListUsers/SetAccess/GetUser -- reverting writeAPIDomainError to a raw err.Error() write in handleListUsers makes this test fail as expected; (2) assertInvalidRequest, now checking the fixed 'invalid_request' slug plus absence of parser text, genuinely catches a reversion to writeAPIError(w,400,err.Error()) in handleSetAccess's decodeJSON branch -- all three UnknownField/MissingGrantedField/EmptyBody 400 tests failed on the mutation; (3) TestNewMux_ConfigValuesReachMiddleware in cmd/main_test.go genuinely exercises the real cfg-to-RouteDeps wiring in newMux (not a hand-built RouteDeps), observing behavioral differences for both CookieSecure and AllowedOrigins across the real production mux; and removing Decision 18's isAdminUserLogin condition from normalizePath makes TestNormalizePath_AdminUsersLoginCollapses/AdminUsersCardinalityIsBounded fail as expected. The 2 minor design findings (AccessService.ListUsers unit test, CONTACT_EMAIL env-to-Config test) are both now present and substantive (TestAccessService_ListUsers_PassesRecordsThroughUnmodified/RepositoryFailureIsPropagated in service/access_test.go; TestLoad_ContactEmail in the new config_test.go). BuildRoutes is confirmed to be the single shared assembly function: routeFixture in access_test.go/middleware_test.go calls handler.BuildRoutes(RouteDeps{...}) directly, and cmd/main.go's newMux delegates to the identical handler.BuildRoutes -- verified by reading routes.go, main.go, and main_test.go's testMux side by side. Negative-path tests consistently assert state-unchanged (accessSnapshot/assertAccessUnchanged), not just status codes, satisfying the task's repeated edge-case requirement. One minor, non-blocking gap remains: a whitespace-only {login} path segment reaching handleSetAccess through the real HTTP route is untested at the integration level (only covered indirectly by the service-layer unit test for AccessService.SetAccess with a blank login).

findings.location: server/internal/handler/access_test.go (no case for a whitespace-only {login} segment reaching the real route); server/internal/service/access.go:241-254 (requireLogin trims and rejects blank logins)
findings.issue: handleSetAccess passes r.PathValue("login") straight to AccessService.SetAccess without its own validation; the blank-login guard lives entirely in service.requireLogin. That guard is unit-tested directly against AccessService (TestAccessService_InvalidArguments_ReturnErrInvalidArgumentWithoutRepoCalls/"SetAccess с пробельным логином"), and confirmed manually here that Go's ServeMux does route a URL-encoded space (e.g. /api/v1/admin/users/%20/access) to the {login} handler with login=" " rather than 404ing it away (unlike a genuinely empty segment via a double slash, which the stdlib mux 404s before any handler runs). No test in access_test.go/middleware_test.go exercises this specific HTTP-layer path, so a hypothetical regression that bypasses or short-circuits AccessService.SetAccess's requireLogin call for whitespace-only logins specifically at the handler layer (e.g. a future refactor that reads login before calling the service and takes a different branch for it) would not be caught by any test running through BuildRoutes. This is a genuinely low-severity gap: the underlying rule is proven correct by the service-level unit test, and the handler introduces no logic of its own on this path (it does not transform, trim, or special-case the login value before passing it through) -- there is no realistic mutation of AccessHandler itself, only of AccessService, that this gap would fail to catch elsewhere.
findings.recommendation: Optional: add one subtest to TestSetAccess_UnknownField400-style tests or a new small test asserting POST /api/v1/admin/users/%20/access as an admin returns 400/invalid_request and leaves state unchanged, exercising the real route end-to-end rather than only the service unit test. Not blocking -- the existing service-level coverage already locks in the correct behavior; this would only close a redundancy gap between layers, not an actual untested behavior.

litmusTest.note: All 16 named TDD-Anchor tests verified present and behaviorally correct. 3 of them were additionally confirmed via live mutation-and-revert: TestAccessHandler_RepositoryFailureAfterGatePasses (mutated handleListUsers to leak err.Error() -> test failed as expected), TestSetAccess_UnknownField400/MissingGrantedField400/EmptyBody400 via assertInvalidRequest (mutated handleSetAccess's decodeJSON branch to writeAPIError(w,400,err.Error()) -> all 3 tests failed as expected), TestNormalizePath_AdminUsersLoginCollapses/AdminUsersCardinalityIsBounded (removed isAdminUserLogin from normalizePath's condition -> both failed as expected). All mutations reverted byte-identical, confirmed via git diff showing only the pre-existing baseline Task-5 diff.

designReviewFollowUp.major_1_leak_test_not_reaching_handler_c: CONFIRMED FIXED. stubUserRepo gained getErrByLogin (per-login) and listErr/setAccessErr (call-specific) fields distinct from the unconditional getErr. New test TestAccessHandler_RepositoryFailureAfterGatePasses sets these so the calling admin's own gate-check GetUser succeeds while the handler's own downstream call fails, genuinely exercising AccessHandler.handleListUsers/handleSetAccess's own writeAPIDomainError wiring. Verified via mutation (see litmusTest note).
designReviewFollowUp.major_2_400_body_only_status_checked: CONFIRMED FIXED. assertInvalidRequest (middleware_test.go:768) now asserts errorCode == 'invalid_request' and containsAny(...) for parser leak strings ('unknown field', 'invalid json', 'json:', 'cannot unmarshal', 'EOF'). All three UnknownField/MissingGrantedField/EmptyBody tests route through it. Verified via mutation.
designReviewFollowUp.major_3_cfg_wiring_untested: CONFIRMED FIXED. cmd/main_test.go added TestNewMux_ConfigValuesReachMiddleware, which builds cfg with varying CookieSecure and AllowedOrigins (CSV with whitespace/trailing comma) and asserts through the real newMux -> handler.BuildRoutes chain that these values reach RequireSameOrigin's behavior. This is exactly the seam design review flagged as unverifiable at design time -- now closed with behavioral (not structural) assertions.
designReviewFollowUp.minor_4_ListUsers_no_unit_test: CONFIRMED FIXED. service/access_test.go added TestAccessService_ListUsers_PassesRecordsThroughUnmodified (raw pass-through, no Decision 10 transformation) and TestAccessService_ListUsers_RepositoryFailureIsPropagated (errors.Is check, not swallowed).
designReviewFollowUp.minor_5_config_test_missing: CONFIRMED FIXED. New server/internal/config/config_test.go added with TestLoad_ContactEmail covering both the env-set and default-empty branches via real config.Load(), using t.Chdir(t.TempDir()) to avoid a developer's local .env leaking into the default-empty assertion.
